claims.text: An actively learned machine-learning interatomic potential trained on ab initio liquid configurations can serve as a substantially better thermodynamic-integration reference than a conventional EAM potential.
Such a machine-learning potential can capture the full diversity of local atomic environments in liquid and near-melting solid high-entropy alloys.
The proposed target materials are multicomponent, for example equimolar five-component, high-entropy alloys in both solid and liquid states near melting.
The reference potential should be actively trained on high-temperature ab initio configurations sampled around melting.
The method is applicable to refractory high-entropy alloys over approximately 0.9–1.1 times their melting temperature.
The method is tailored to multicomponent, near-equimolar compositions with strong chemical disorder.
The machine-learning potential provides a smoother and more accurate representation of varying local atomic environments than EAM.
The varying local atomic environments represented by the potential are equivalent to configurational entropy.
More accurate representation of local environments improves reference–target phase-space overlap in both liquid and near-melting solid phases.
EAM models have limited ability to represent the many-body and chemical complexity of multicomponent high-entropy-alloy liquids.
Actively learned moment-tensor potentials can be parameterized using ab initio data for refractory multicomponent alloys.
Active ab initio training enables the potential to capture a broader range of atomic configurations.
Broader coverage of atomic configurations reduces mismatch along the thermodynamic-integration path.
Reducing thermodynamic-integration path mismatch improves computed free-energy differences.
Relative to TOR-TILD EAM references, the proposed potential will reduce integration errors by roughly 30–50%.
TOR-TILD uses conventional EAM references that inadequately sample the configurational space of ab initio high-entropy-alloy liquids.
The intervention may be less effective for systems with chemical heterogeneity beyond typical five-component alloys.
The intervention may be less effective at lower temperatures when vibrational contributions dominate the free-energy error.
Displacement-covariance vibrational-entropy analysis can provide an independent ab initio free-energy benchmark for the proposed solid-and-liquid comparison.

Failure to obtain a statistically significant reduction, exemplified as less than 10% improvement in path mismatch, or failure to move the free energy closer to the benchmark would falsify the hypothesis.
